note: Sat 22 Aug 2026, ~08:20 SGT. Weekend run — US/HK/SG markets closed; latest completed sessions Fri 21 Aug (US/HK/SG) and Thu 20 Aug (JP/KR). Builds on the prior edition (through Thu 20 Aug) with Friday's continuation and confirmation: gold hit a fresh three-month high ($4,661.70), Friday was a genuine equity-market rebound (S&P/Dow/Nasdaq all +0.4-1.0%, VIX back to 15.13) after Thursday's AI-capex selloff, the Iran conflict escalated further (UAE severed trade ties with Tehran; vessel-tracking data shows Iran still controls Hormuz shipping), US national debt crossed $40T, and Bitcoin's Thursday close ($73,032.76, verified) continued to a ~$77,863 weekend level (a live quote, not a close — flagged as such after the prior edition mistakenly asserted an unverifiable $74,859 figure). The master catalyst thread (Treasury buyback → gold/silver breakout → KOSPI round-trip → Bitcoin surge, items #1-3+#6 below) still holds together.

items.headline: US Treasury doubles long-end bond buybacks — the single biggest cross-asset catalyst of the two sessions
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Bessent announced the Treasury is at least doubling its liquidity-support buyback operations for 10-30yr securities (from $2bn to $4bn per operation), starting 9 Sep, after the 30yr yield hit a post-2007 high (~5.33%) on federal-debt concerns. Gross US national debt officially crossed $40 trillion on 20 Aug — the fastest trillion-dollar increment on record, just five months after $39T — with debt-service costs now exceeding the defense budget. The buyback announcement pulled the 10yr to 4.647% and the 30yr to 5.196%, and was widely read as a return to monetary accommodation.
items.actionable: This buyback is the common thread behind Wed's real gold/silver breakout, Thu's KOSPI rebound, and the Bitcoin surge — a liquidity/debasement trade, not a growth story. Supportive for the silver/gold miners sleeve; confirms the big-cash-pile thesis (real yields falling) even as equities wobbled Thursday.

items.headline: KOSPI's near-perfect 2-day round trip explained: chip-stock crash (Wed) then buyback-fueled rebound (Thu)
items.summary: KOSPI fell 5.80% Wed 19 Aug (Samsung -7.82%, SK Hynix -9.75%) on a US 30-year Treasury yield spike to a 19-year high plus a Philadelphia Semiconductor Index -5% US selloff the prior session, triggering a program-sell halt. Thu 20 Aug it surged 5.89% (nearly erasing the drop) after Samsung and SK Hynix announced massive capital-return plans (>KRW100tn and ~KRW40tn respectively) and the Treasury buyback (item #1) eased bond-yield fears.
items.actionable: A leveraged, yield-driven chip-sector round trip, not a structural anomaly — a preview of how violently HK tech (Tencent/SMIC, similarly AI-capex-exposed) can swing on the same yield/AI-capex-jitters axis; treat single-day HSI/SMIC moves this week with the same lens.

items.headline: Gold/silver breakout extends into Friday: gold hits a three-month high (~$4,661.70) as the rally proves durable, not a one-off
items.summary: Gold and silver rallied sharply (GLD +3.84%, SLV +4.47%) Wed 19 Aug as the Treasury buyback news pulled real yields down ahead of the FOMC minutes release, while a weaker dollar amplified gains for foreign buyers; miners outperformed (GDX +9.42%, SILJ +9.55%, Barrick +8.82%). The move continued into Friday 21 Aug, with gold futures up a further ~2% to a three-month high of $4,661.70/oz (spot ~$4,633.90) on continued dollar weakness and the fresh $40T debt milestone, closing the week +1.97% on Friday per market data.
items.actionable: Confirms this is a genuine, multi-day rates/debasement-driven breakout rather than a one-off headline spike — unlike Monday 17 Aug's futures-roll artifact that was corrected in the prior brief. Friday's fresh three-month high argues for holding the position into further Fed dovish repricing and Jackson Hole (27-29 Aug), though Thursday's miner deceleration (GDX +2.59%) shows the sleeve is also now sensitive to broader equity risk-off.

items.headline: Thursday's US equity selloff (S&P -0.87%, VIX +7.52%) driven by AI-capex balance-sheet fears, not rates
items.summary: The WSJ flagged roughly $3 trillion of off-balance-sheet AI infrastructure commitments across nine major tech names, reviving 'AI bubble' concerns even as the 30yr yield eased post-buyback. VIX jumped over 7% to 16.01 and the 10yr climbed toward 4.70% intraday. Rare-earth names caught in the same downdraft: MP Materials -2.89%, Energy Fuels -6.40%.
items.actionable: An AI-capex-credibility scare, structurally different from Wednesday's rates-driven metals rally — expect continued volatility in rare-earth/AI-adjacent names (MP, UUUU) independent of the gold/silver trend; staying out of AI-capex-linked equities near-term is consistent with the big-cash-pile positioning.

items.headline: Rare-earth names reverse sharply higher (MP +9.10%, UUUU +8.92%) on G7 non-China supply-chain push and US government-backed financing
items.summary: Friday's rare-earth rally reversed Thursday's AI-fear-driven selloff on three concrete policy catalysts: G7 leaders agreed to cut reliance on non-bloc (i.e. China) rare-earth suppliers, the Pentagon backed a $500M loan to Phoenix Tailings, and the Department of Energy selected seven critical-mineral processing/battery projects for support. Materials was the S&P 500's strongest sector on the day (+2.09%).
items.actionable: A genuine, government-policy-driven catalyst distinct from Thursday's sentiment-only selloff — reinforces the ex-China rare-earth re-rating thesis (MP, Lynas, USA Rare Earth, Energy Fuels) underlying the watchlist, independent of the AI-capex-fear cycle.

items.headline: July FOMC minutes lean hawkish: three regional presidents dissented for a hike, not a cut
items.summary: Minutes from the 28-29 July meeting (rates held at 3.50-3.75%) showed three regional Fed presidents (Logan, Hammack, Kashkari) dissented in favor of a 25bp hike, with the Committee focused on inflation persistence. New Fed Chair Warsh also floated moving to 6 meetings/year.
items.actionable: The metals rally happened despite hawkish minutes, purely on the Treasury buyback/liquidity story — a reminder the gold/silver trade is now a debt-monetization trade, decoupled from the Fed's own rate rhetoric. Don't expect the minutes' hawkishness to cap gold near-term.

items.headline: Bitcoin closes Thursday +5.44% at $73,033, then keeps climbing over the weekend to a ~$77,863 level
items.summary: Bitcoin's verified Thursday 20 Aug close was $73,032.76 (+5.44%), the second straight double-digit-percent two-day advance after Wednesday's Treasury-buyback-driven +7.09% (to $69,266.19). Crypto trades continuously, so Saturday 22 Aug SGT shows a further move to a ~$77,862.74 level — this is a live quote, not a session close, and is reported as such. The Treasury buyback was read as monetary debasement, fueling a 'digital gold' bid; Trump met crypto executives pushing the CLARITY Act and floated a US strategic Bitcoin reserve, alongside a reported multi-billion-dollar short-position liquidation cascade.
items.actionable: Bitcoin's move is a levered, liquidation-driven amplification of the same liquidity/debasement narrative driving gold — correlated risk, not a diversifier, for the precious-metals thesis this week. Next catalysts: the Sept 15 CLARITY Act vote and Jackson Hole (Aug 27-29).

items.headline: Iran conflict escalates sharply: ADNOC tankers attacked, Trump declares economic 'D-Day', UAE severs ties, and data shows Iran still controls Hormuz shipping
items.summary: Two ADNOC vessels were attacked transiting the Strait of Hormuz Thu evening (one crew death). Trump announced sweeping new sanctions on Iran's oil, shipping and financial sectors plus a continued naval blockade (19-20 Aug), calling it the 'most crushing economic operation ever' against Iran and threatening sanctions on any nation still trading with Tehran. The UAE — Iran's #2 trade partner after China — then suspended all trade and financial transactions with Iran after its air defenses intercepted two ballistic missiles it says were launched from Iranian territory (one landed in UAE waters; Iran denies responsibility). Separately, an Al Jazeera vessel-tracking analysis (1-19 Aug) found Iran retains de facto control of Hormuz shipping despite the US naval presence: of 112 oil/gas carriers, 21 openly used Iran's mandated northern route versus just 2 using the US/Oman-backed route, with over 60% of all traffic now going dark or unclassified.
items.actionable: A live, widening, unresolved war-risk premium in both oil and gold — the UAE trade rupture and vessel-tracking data show this is structural escalation, not a headline blip, arguing for keeping the precious-metals hedge sized for a prolonged elevated-risk regime rather than trimming into strength. Monitor for a Hormuz closure escalation as a tail risk to HK tech/SGX shipping-adjacent names.

items.headline: Alibaba fiscal Q1: revenue beats, profit misses on 75% YoY AI capex surge; rare HK$10.4bn southbound outflow
items.summary: Alibaba reported revenue of RMB268.95bn (+9% YoY, beat) but adjusted net profit of RMB20.72bn missed estimates (vs RMB25.58bn expected) as capex hit RMB67.68bn (+75% YoY) on AI infrastructure spend. Mainland investors made contrarian net additions to Alibaba (HK$2.21bn) even as Hong Kong saw a rare HK$10.4bn single-day southbound net outflow.
items.actionable: The AI-capex-driven margin compression mirrors the US 'off-balance-sheet AI commitments' scare (item #4) playing out in HK tech — the contrarian mainland dip-buying is worth tracking as a read on HK tech risk appetite generally.

items.headline: Tencent Q2 capex up 176% YoY to RMB52.8bn on AI spend; shares +1.08% Wed to 447.20
items.summary: Tencent's capital expenditure surged 176% YoY to RMB52.8 billion as it ramps AI infrastructure investment, testing investor patience with the bullish thesis even as shares rose modestly Wed (+1.08% to HK$447.20, market cap $508.6bn) and continued higher Thu (+0.94% to 451.40).
items.actionable: Consistent with the broader AI-capex-scrutiny theme — HK tech capex intensity is now a two-sided risk (growth story vs margin/FCF concern); watch for further capex-driven volatility across the Hang Seng Tech complex.

items.headline: Singapore banks post record/near-record Q2 2026 profits; OCBC crosses S$30 for the first time
items.summary: DBS (S$3.08bn, +9%), OCBC (S$2.22bn, +22%, record) and UOB (S$1.48bn, +10%) all beat estimates, driven by fee/wealth-management income rather than lending margins. OCBC and DBS trade at all-time highs; UOB lags on NIM compression (1.74%, -8bp), cut fee-income guidance, and is divesting UOB Asset Management (announced 5 Aug).
items.actionable: SGX bank strength (OCBC/DBS momentum) is a structural positive for the owner's largest exposure sleeve independent of this week's volatility; UOB's relative weakness warrants closer monitoring versus peers.

items.headline: OCBC Research turns selective on S-REITs as the sector lags the bank-led STI sharply YTD
items.summary: OCBC Group Research maintained a selective stance on S-REITs, citing rate-hike concerns and elevated long-end yields; the iEdge S-REIT Index has returned -3.3% YTD versus +26.8% for the STI, a gap driven almost entirely by the bank rally. Top picks flagged: CapitaLand Ascendas REIT, CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust, Keppel DC REIT, CapitaLand India Trust.
items.actionable: Quantifies a divergence already implicit in this book — SGX banks near record highs while REITs lag badly on rate concerns. If adding to the SGX REIT sleeve, this argues for being selective (data-centre/industrial names) rather than broad REIT beta.

items.headline: Jackson Hole Symposium (27-29 Aug) — new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first keynote lands Fri 28 Aug
items.summary: Jackson Hole runs 27-29 Aug with Kevin Warsh delivering his first keynote as Fed Chair on Fri 28 Aug (official theme: payments, but labor-market weakness and inflation are expected to dominate). Lands 19 days before the 16 Sep FOMC decision.
items.actionable: The next major scheduled catalyst for gold/silver and rates — given Warsh's dissent history favored hikes over cuts, his tone could either validate or puncture the current liquidity/debasement rally in metals and Bitcoin. Size gold/silver-miner positioning with this event in mind.
